title.en: Six ways people have used magic to protect their homes throughout history—from witch bottles to 'hag stones'
title.zh: 六种历史上人们用来保护家园的魔法——从巫术瓶到“女巫石”

summary.en: The article examines the historical use of magic, such as witch bottles and hag stones, across various cultures and eras as a means of protecting homes and their inhabitants. It highlights magic's diverse forms and functions as a fundamental aspect of human life and a subject of ongoing historical and archaeological...
summary.zh: 本文探讨了在不同文化和时代，人们如何使用巫术瓶和“女巫石”等魔法来保护房屋及其居民。文章强调了魔法的多种形式和功能，认为它是人类生活的一个基本方面，也是历史和考古学研究的持续课题。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

Virtually all cultures and eras fizz with magic. You might call it a secret ingredient of human life because magic takes so many forms and serves so many functions.

One relatively new area of research among historians and archaeologists focuses on the use of magic and mysticism to protect buildings, gardens and their inhabitants . It's one of the many forms of magic I explore in my new book, Magick: Decoding the Visual Culture of Spells, Illusions and Psychic Powers .

Early modern Europe saw numerous reports of towns, such as Schiltach, Germany, in 1533, being burned by "incendiary witchcraft" and fire-starting demons. These dramatic examples, from an era of terrifyingly combustible homes, help explain why so many people focused magical building protection on chimneys and hearths.

Even today, people living comparatively safe and comfortable lives still use special objects and occult techniques to allay their anxieties and increase their sense of security.

A few years ago, a lovely volunteer guiding me around an ancient church in North Yorkshire explained she had planted a rowan tree in her garden. The purpose? To repel her neighbor's "evil eye." Rowan trees have been used in this way for centuries across the British Isles.

So, if you've got problem neighbors, or your house and garden seem to suffer from bad luck, perhaps it's time to try a magical solution.

Trees, herbs and other plants were and are used to defend properties against dangers both natural and supernatural. The 17th-century botanist Nicholas Culpeper's Complete Herbal (1653) claimed that a bay tree in the garden protects against witchcraft, the devil and lightning.

Betony , meanwhile, was said to be good against liver disease, epidemics and witchcraft, while bittersweet nightshade was believed to be effective against harmful sorcery.

Across Britain and Europe, a rosemary bush in the garden was supposed to protect against harmful night witches, who would be caught counting every leaf until the morning light dispelled their evil powers. In the Americas, chili peppers have long been regarded as evil-averting and were sometimes fixed to doors to repel harmful powers.

In early modern Europe and beyond, five- and six-pointed stars were inscribed into wood and mortar to repel evil.

Magical instructional texts known today as "grimoires"—including the tiny Booke of Experiments (1622), now held in Oxford's Bodleian Library—explain that these star symbols helped overcome enemies.

Some inscriptions may have been masons' marks to assist construction. However, the concentration of these symbols in certain...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 几乎所有文化和时代都充满了魔法。你可以称它为人类生命的秘密成分，因为魔法有多种形式并具有多种功能。 历史学家和考古学家的一个相对较新的研究领域集中在使用魔法和神秘主义来保护建筑物、花园及其居民。这是我在新书《Magick：解码咒语、幻象和心灵力量的视觉文化》中探索的多种魔法形式之一。 现代早期的欧洲有许多关于城镇的报道，例如 1533 年德国希尔塔赫 (Schiltach)，被“燃烧巫术”和引火恶魔烧毁。这些戏剧性的例子来自一个可怕的易燃房屋时代，有助于解释为什么这么多人将魔法建筑保护的重点放在烟囱和壁炉上。 即使在今天，人们过着相对安全舒适的生活，仍然使用特殊的物品和神秘的技术来缓解他们的焦虑，增加他们的安全感。 几年前，一位可爱的志愿者带我参观了北约克郡的一座古老教堂，她解释说她在她的花园里种了一棵花楸树。目的？为了击退邻居的“邪恶之眼”。几个世纪以来，不列颠群岛一直以这种方式使用罗文树。 所以，如果你的邻居有问题，或者你的房子和花园似乎运气不好，也许是时候尝试一个神奇的解决方案了。 树木、草本植物和其他植物过去和现在都被用来保护财产免受自然和超自然的危险。 17 世纪的植物学家尼古拉斯·卡尔佩珀 (Nicholas Culpeper) 在其《草药大全》(1653) 中声称，花园中的月桂树可以抵御巫术、魔鬼和闪电。 与此同时，据说贝托尼能有效对抗肝病、流行病和巫术，而苦乐参半的茄属植物被认为能有效对抗有害巫术。 在英国和欧洲，花园里的迷迭香丛被认为可以防止有害的夜间女巫，这些女巫会被发现数着每一片叶子，直到晨光驱散她们的邪恶力量。在美洲，辣椒长期以来被认为具有避邪作用，有时被固定在门上以驱除有害力量。 在近代早期的欧洲及其他地区，五角星和六角星被刻在木头和灰泥上以驱除邪恶。 今天被称为“魔法书”的魔法教学文本——包括现在保存在牛津大学博德利图书馆的小《实验之书》（1622 年）——解释了这些星星符号有助于战胜敌人。 一些铭文可能是泥瓦匠帮助建造的标记。然而，这些符号集中在某些......

reflection.en: From ancient witch bottles to modern-day rituals, humans have consistently sought ways to safeguard their homes and loved ones. This enduring impulse to understand and protect reflects a deep-seated desire for security and order in a sometimes unpredictable world. Proverbs 18:15 reminds us that the pursuit of knowledge is the foundation of wisdom, a...
reflection.zh: 从古老的巫术瓶到现代的仪式，人类一直在寻求保护家园和亲人的方法。这种对理解和保护的持久冲动，反映了在有时不可预测的世界中对安全和秩序的深层渴望。《箴言》18:15提醒我们，追求知识是智慧的基础，这一原则贯穿于人类创造安全避难所的各种尝试之中。

verse.textEn: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.
verse.textZh: 聪明人的心得知识；智慧人的耳求知识。

title.en: Fossilized 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth found by California scientist
title.zh: 科学家发现一万年前乳齿象牙齿化石

summary.en: A California scientist has discovered a 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth in 'immaculate condition' in San Mateo County. The molar from the large mammal, which once roamed North America, was found by geomorphologist Brigid Lynch while working at a preserve.
summary.zh: 一位加州科学家在圣马特奥县发现了一颗保存完好的1万年前的乳齿象牙齿化石。这颗属于曾漫步于北美的大型哺乳动物的臼齿，是由地貌学家布里吉德·林奇在保护区工作时发现的。

body.en: Molar from large mammal that once lived in North America is in ‘immaculate condition’ after discovery in Bay Area A 10,000 year-old tooth in remarkable condition from an ancient Pacific mastodon, a large mammal that once inhabited North America, was recently discovered by a California scientist. Brigid Lynch, a geomorphologist, was working at a preserve in San Mateo county, when she stumbled across a peculiar rock. Continue reading...
body.zh: 湾区发现的曾经生活在北美的大型哺乳动物的臼齿在湾区被发现后仍处于“完美状态”最近，加州的一位科学家发现了一颗古老的太平洋乳齿象的牙齿，其状态非常好。太平洋乳齿象是一种曾经生活在北美的大型哺乳动物。地貌学家布里吉德·林奇 (Brigid Lynch) 在圣马特奥县的一个保护区工作时，偶然发现了一块奇特的岩石。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of this ancient mastodon tooth is a tangible link to a distant past, reminding us of the vastness of time and the creatures that once inhabited our world. It speaks to the deep wisdom embedded in creation, waiting to be uncovered through careful observation and scientific inquiry.
reflection.zh: 这颗古老的乳齿象牙齿化石的发现，是通往遥远过去的切实联系，提醒我们时间的浩瀚以及曾经栖息在我们世界上的生物。它体现了造物中蕴含的深刻智慧，等待着通过细致的观察和科学的探索而被揭示。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: CERN finds gluons behaving strangely deep inside atomic nuclei
title.zh: CERN在原子核深处发现胶子行为异常

summary.en: Physicists at CERN have discovered a novel method to examine the interior of atomic nuclei, helping to differentiate between two competing theories on gluon behavior. Utilizing the ALICE experiment at the Large Hadron Collider, researchers achieved unparalleled spatial resolution in measuring particle production,...
summary.zh: 欧洲核子研究组织（CERN）的物理学家发现了一种新的方法来探测原子核的内部，并区分关于胶子行为的两种竞争性解释。研究人员利用大型强子对撞机上的ALICE实验，以前所未有的空间分辨率测量了粒子产生，揭示了小至质子四分之一大小的结构。他们观察到在最小尺度上，J/ψ粒子的产生量出人意料地下降，这使得传统的“核影效应”难以解释...

body.en: Physicists at CERN have found a new way to peer deep inside atomic nuclei and distinguish between two competing explanations for how gluons behave. Using the ALICE experiment at the Large Hadron Collider, researchers measured particle production at unprecedented spatial resolution, revealing structures as small as about one-quarter the size of a proton. At the smallest scales, they saw a surprising drop in J/ψ production that conventional “nuclear shadowing” struggles to explain.
body.zh: 欧洲核子研究中心的物理学家找到了一种新方法，可以深入观察原子核内部，并区分对胶子行为的两种相互竞争的解释。研究人员利用大型强子对撞机的 ALICE 实验，以前所未有的空间分辨率测量了粒子的产生，揭示了小至质子四分之一大小的结构。在最小的尺度上，他们发现 J/ψ 的产生令人惊讶地下降，这是传统的“核阴影”难以解释的。

reflection.en: The universe, from the vastness of space to the heart of the atom, is a testament to Yahweh’s intricate design. As scientists at CERN delve deeper into the subatomic realm, they uncover more of creation’s profound order and mystery. This pursuit of knowledge, grounded in observing the physical world, echoes the ancient wisdom that creation itself speaks of...
reflection.zh: 宇宙从浩瀚的空间到原子的核心，都见证了雅伟精妙的创造。当欧洲核子研究组织的科学家们深入亚原子领域时，他们揭示了更多关于被造界深刻的秩序和奥秘。这种以观察物质世界为基础的求知探索，呼应了古老的智慧——被造界本身就诉说着其创造者的能力和智慧。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger
title.zh: 法国创纪录热浪或将使香槟酒精度数升高

summary.en: Record heatwaves in France have resulted in an unusual harvest with sweeter grapes, allowing winemakers to potentially produce champagne with up to 15% alcohol by volume, an increase from the usual 13% cap. This phenomenon, driven by extreme heat and drought, could become more common due to climate change, leading to...
summary.zh: 法国创纪录的热浪导致了异常的丰收，出产的葡萄糖分更高，使得酿酒商能够生产酒精度高达15%的香槟酒，高于通常13%的上限。这种极端高温和干旱造成的现象，可能因气候变化而变得更加普遍，导致收获季节提前。

body.en:
Champagne lovers may find themselves getting tipsy more quickly after French producers have been given the go-ahead to raise the alcohol content in a bottle of bubbly for the first time following this summer's record heatwave.

Winemakers can temporarily produce champagne with an alcohol content of up to 15% - above the 13% cap, industry officials have said.

The extreme heat and drought produced grapes with exceptionally higher sugar levels. Yeast converts sugar into alcohol during fermentation.

France's Champagne region also saw its earliest-ever harvest due to the weather, something that could become the norm "in 10 to 15 years" because of climate change, according to the Comite Champagne industry association.

The temporary increase in champagne's alcohol content is only expected to affect a small number of wines, a spokeswoman for the Comite Champagne told the BBC.

During the second fermentation process, which gives champagne its bubbles, "a very small number of wines from this harvest could have slightly exceeded the regulatory limit of 13%, reaching around 13.1% or 13.2%".

"Therefore a decision was made to exceptionally and temporarily increase the regulatory limit to 15% - only for this year," she said.

The first grapes were cut in early August and the harvest expanded by the middle of the month, "the earliest ever recorded in Champagne", the association said.

"The 2026 growing season will be remembered as one of the most unusual in Champagne's history, marked by severe spring frosts of historic intensity, an exceptionally early flowering period and five heatwaves throughout the summer." it added.

Speaking in the Times newspaper, Stéphane Vignon, a producer in Verzenay said: "The Mediterranean climate is moving north. This is year one of a new cycle. It's unlikely to be every year, but it will happen again".

Higher-strength champagne is unlikely to be an obvious selling point, warned Jane Anson, a wine columnist and author based in Bordeaux.

"The battle between what consumers want and what nature provides must be very stressful for producers."

The 2026 vintage is unlikely to hit shelves until 2028 as champagne must age for at least 15 months.

Maxime Toubart, co-chair of the Comite Champagne, told the AFP news agency that the likelihood of hotter weather in the future means "this unusual harvest will probably become the norm in 10 to 15 years".

France has been one of Europe's worst-hit countries during this year's extreme weather, sparking huge wildfires .

Climate change is driving up global average temperatures, making heatwaves more frequent and intense.

It has been felt acutely in Europe, which is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service. ,...
body.zh: 在今年夏天创纪录的热浪之后，法国生产商首次获准提高一瓶起泡酒的酒精含量，香槟爱好者可能会发现自己更快地喝醉。 行业官员表示，酿酒师可以暂时生产酒精含量高达 15% 的香槟，高于 13% 的上限。 极端炎热和干旱使得葡萄的糖分含量异常高。酵母在发酵过程中将糖转化为酒精。 据法国香槟行业协会称，由于天气原因，法国香槟地区也迎来了有史以来最早的收获期，由于气候变化，这可能会在“10到15年内”成为常态。 香槟委员会发言人告诉英国广播公司，香槟酒精含量的暂时增加预计只会影响少数葡萄酒。 在第二次发酵过程中，香槟产生了气泡，“本次收获的极少数葡萄酒可能会略微超过13%的监管限值，达到约13.1%或13.2%”。 她说：“因此，我们决定暂时将监管上限提高到 15%，仅限今年。” 该协会表示，第一批葡萄于八月初收获，到月中旬收获量扩大，这是“香槟地区有史以来最早的收获”。 “2026 年的生长季节将被铭记为香槟历史上最不寻常的季节之一，其特点是历史性强度的严重春季霜冻、异常提前的花期以及整个夏季的五次热浪。”它补充道。 韦尔泽奈的制片人斯特凡·维尼翁 (Stéphane Vignon) 在《泰晤士报》上发表讲话时表示：“地中海气候正在向北移动。这是新周期的第一年。不太可能每年都这样，但它会再次发生”。 波尔多葡萄酒专栏作家兼作家简·安森警告说，高浓度香槟不太可能成为一个明显的卖点。 “消费者想要的东西和大自然提供的东西之间的斗争对生产者来说肯定是非常有压力的。” 2026 年年份的香槟要到 2028 年才能上架，因为香槟必须陈酿至少 15 个月。 香槟委员会联合主席马克西姆·图巴特 (Maxime Toubart) 告诉法新社，未来天气可能会变得更热，这意味着“这种不寻常的收获可能会在 10 到 15 年内成为常态”。 法国是今年极端天气中受灾最严重的欧洲国家之一，引发了巨大的野火。 气候变化正在推高全球平均气温，使热浪更加频繁和强烈。 根据哥白尼气候服务机构的数据，欧洲对此的感受最为强烈，欧洲是变暖最快的大陆，升温速度是全球平均水平的两倍。 ,...

reflection.en: The earth is full of your riches; this is that great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts. The current heatwaves in France, while challenging, have yielded grapes with higher sugar content, leading to a potential increase in champagne's alcohol. This serves as a reminder of the intricate and often surprising...
reflection.zh: 雅伟啊，你的物产何其丰盛，这广阔无垠的海洋，其中有无数的爬物，大大小小的活物。法国当前的热浪虽然带来了挑战，却也产出了糖分更高的葡萄，可能使香槟酒的酒精度数升高。这提醒我们，即使在气候变化之中，雅伟的智慧也以各种精妙且出人意料的方式体现在自然界中。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: ‘Immature playground boasting’: Mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp
title.zh: “不成熟的游乐场吹嘘”：数学家们对OpenAI的最新成就感到不安

summary.en: As an OpenAI model cracks a Millennium Prize Problem that has puzzled experts for decades, many are shocked by the pace of change. The achievement involved a massive computational effort, raising questions about the future of mathematical discovery.
summary.zh: 随着OpenAI模型破解了困扰专家数十年的千禧年大奖难题，许多人对变革的速度感到震惊。这项成就涉及巨大的计算投入，引发了关于数学发现未来的疑问。

body.en: As OpenAI model cracks Millennium Prize Problem that puzzled experts for decades, many feel shocked at pace of change It was a week that left mathematicians reeling. Hot on the heels of a flurry of cases of artificial intelligence furthering the field , OpenAI declared a major scalp: its latest AI model had cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, a puzzle with a $1m reward that had defied human brains for decades. The achievement bore little resemblance to how mathematical problems normally fall. A near-trillion dollar private company had unleashed 10,000 agents – AI systems that carry out tasks autonomously – on the problem. The bill was estimated at $15m. Continue reading...
body.zh: 随着 OpenAI 模型破解了困扰专家数十年的千年奖难题，许多人对变化的速度感到震惊，这一周让数学家们感到震惊。继人工智能领域出现一系列进一步发展的案例之后，OpenAI 宣布了一项重大举措：其最新的人工智能模型破解了千年奖难题，这是一个悬赏 100 万美元的难题，数十年来一直挑战人类大脑。这一成就与数学问题通常的解决方式几乎没有相似之处。一家价值近万亿美元的私营公司部署了 10,000 个代理（自主执行任务的人工智能系统）来解决这个问题。该账单估计为 1500 万美元。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid progress of artificial intelligence, exemplified by OpenAI's AI cracking a Millennium Prize Problem, reflects a dramatic acceleration in human knowledge. Daniel 12:4 speaks of knowledge increasing in the end times, a phenomenon we are witnessing today with technologies like AI. This surge in capability calls for wisdom and discernment, ensuring...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展，以OpenAI的AI破解千禧年大奖难题为例，反映了人类知识的急剧加速。但以理书12:4预言知识在末世将大大增长，这正是我们今天通过人工智能等技术所目睹的现象。这种能力的激增需要智慧和分辨力，以确保日益增长的知识能服务于人类的最佳利益。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs
title.zh: 拯救古老沼泽的缓慢而泥泞的工作

summary.en: Sarah Hickey and her team are engaged in the meticulous and labor-intensive task of restoring and maintaining nearly 20,000 acres of upland peatland on the Isle of Man. Their work involves assessing damaged areas and injecting life back into the peat, which has built up over thousands of years and stores significant...
summary.zh: 莎拉·希基和她的团队正在曼岛进行一项细致且耗时的工作，以恢复和维护近2万英亩的高地泥炭地。他们的工作包括评估受损区域，并为数千年来积累的、储存着大量有机物的泥炭注入生机。

body.en:
High up on a Manx hillside, Sarah Hickey effortlessly pushes a metre-long metal rod into the wet ground until it disappears almost to her hands.

"This is pretty deep here," she says, reading the markings on the probe. Beneath her boots is peat, built up over thousands of years and consisting of partially decayed plants and organic matter.

Hickey is the island's Peatland Officer and part of an Uplands team of just three, who, between them, manage about 8,000 hectares of the Island's hills.

Hickey's job is to find the parts of that landscape which have been damaged, and inject life into it.

Peat is partially decomposed vegetation that builds up in waterlogged ground over centuries, storing more carbon than any other soil on Earth.

"It's important to keep that carbon locked away and not released to the atmosphere," Hickey says.

Much of that carbon has stayed locked away, but not all of it. The island's uplands were largely stripped of trees by the 17th century, and with little timber left to burn, islanders turned to the hills for fuel instead.

Peat would be cut into blocks and left to dry; peat made a good, slow-burning fuel, and for generations it was what Manx households cooked on and heated their homes with.

The practice was banned in 2020, but the bare faces that cutting left behind are still collapsing and eroding today, washing sediment down into reservoirs.

Repairs start with a digger light enough not to cause fresh damage, which pulls the bare peat back to a gentler slope and folds the vegetation over it.

What is left exposed is protected with bio logs, then held down under netting, which keeps the ground shaded and damp so new vegetation can take hold.

It holds huge amounts of water, slowing rain as it moves downhill, reducing flooding and filtering out sediment before it reaches the reservoir.

It is also, she says, more fire-resistant; peat in good condition can be up to 90% water, which is increasingly important as wildfires become more common during summer months.

It matters for wildlife too. Ground-nesting birds such as hen harriers rely on open, treeless bog, safe from predators that would otherwise perch and watch for prey, while the wet ground breeds the invertebrates chicks are fed on.

The reward can arrive fast. After installing coir logs on one site last year, Hickey and colleagues sat down for tea beside the new pools they had created.

"Straight away there were dragonflies in that pool laying eggs," she says. "It was amazing to see what a difference these little features are making."

body.zh: 在马恩岛的山坡上，莎拉·希基毫不费力地将一根一米长的金属棒推入潮湿的地面，直到它几乎消失在她的手中。 “这里相当深，”她一边说，一边读着探头上的标记。她的靴子下面是泥炭，经过数千年的积累，由部分腐烂的植物和有机物组成。 希基是岛上的泥炭地官员，也是高地团队的一员，该团队只有三人，管理着岛上约 8,000 公顷的山丘。 希基的工作是找到景观中被破坏的部分，并为其注入生命。 泥炭是部分分解的植被，几个世纪以来在浸水的土地上形成的，储存的碳比地球上任何其他土壤都多。 “重要的是要锁住这些碳，不要释放到大气中，”希基说。 大部分碳都被锁住了，但不是全部。到了 17 世纪，岛上的高地大部分树木都被砍光了，可供燃烧的木材所剩无几，岛民们转而到山上寻找燃料。 泥炭会被切成块并晾干；泥炭是一种良好的、缓慢燃烧的燃料，马恩岛家庭世世代代都用泥炭做饭和取暖。 这种做法已于 2020 年被禁止，但切割留下的裸露面至今仍在崩塌和侵蚀，将沉积物冲入水库。 修复工作从挖掘机开始，挖掘机的重量要足够轻，不会造成新的损坏，它将裸露的泥炭拉回到较缓的斜坡上，并将植被折叠在上面。 暴露在外的部分用生物原木保护，然后用网固定，使地面保持阴凉和潮湿，以便新的植被生长。 它拥有大量的水，可以减缓降雨向下移动的速度，减少洪水，并在沉积物到达水库之前过滤掉沉积物。 她说，它也更耐火；状况良好的泥炭可含有高达 90% 的水，随着夏季野火变得更加常见，这一点变得越来越重要。 这对野生动物也很重要。母鹞等在地面筑巢的鸟类依靠开阔、无树的沼泽，免受捕食者的侵害，否则它们会栖息和观察猎物，而潮湿的地面则繁殖无脊椎动物雏鸟。 奖励可以很快到达。去年在一个地点安装了椰壳原木后，希基和同事在他们建造的新水池旁边坐下来喝茶。 “立刻就有蜻蜓在那个水池里产卵了，”她说。 “看到这些小功能所带来的改变真是太神奇了。” 在 BBC 上阅读更多来自马恩岛的故事，在 BBC iPlayer 上观看 BBC 西北今晚节目，并在 Facebook、external 和 X, external 上关注 BBC Isle of Man。

reflection.en: The dedicated efforts of Sarah Hickey and her team to restore ancient peatlands exemplify a profound respect for the natural world. This painstaking work, often unseen and unglamorous, mirrors the biblical call to be stewards of creation, recognizing its inherent value and the long-term benefits of its health. It is a testament to the idea that even...
reflection.zh: 莎拉·希基及其团队为恢复古老泥炭地所做的辛勤努力，体现了对自然界的深刻尊重。这项艰苦、不为人知且不引人注目的工作，呼应了圣经中关于管理创造物的呼召，认识到其内在价值及其健康带来的长远益处。它证明了即使是看似微小、缓慢的努力，也能促进雅伟称之为“甚好”的土地的繁荣。

verse.textEn: God saw all that he had made, and it was very good.
verse.textZh: 神看着一切所造的都甚好。

title.en: Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK
title.zh: 拯救英国唯一湖泊中微小黏滑蜗牛的战斗

summary.en: Once prevalent across the UK, this mollusc is now only found in one lake in Wales.
summary.zh: 这种软体动物曾遍布英国各地，但现在仅存于威尔士的一个湖泊中。

body.en:
A tiny snail found in only one lake in the UK has been dubbed as precious as an Egyptian artefact as conservationists bid to save it.

Several British zoos are setting up so-called ark populations of the glutinous snail, one of Europe's rarest species, using creatures bred in a back garden in Ceredigion.

"Beguiled by their cuteness," conservationist Ian Hughes has made it his "life-defining" mission to protect the threatened mollusc, which was once widespread in UK waters.

"There was a point where we'd got more snails in our garden than have ever been seen in the wild," he said.

Myxas glutinosa gets its name from the gooey mantle that covers its extremely delicate, gold-flecked brown shell.

It is no bigger than a fingertip, but has comically large antennae - which Hughes likens to "big floppy ears".

The snails, which feed on algae and are considered an indicator of healthy lakes and rivers, have been driven to extinction across England.

Hughes said the snails were "something to preserve and cherish like Egyptian artefacts".

In the UK, their last known refuge is Wales' largest natural lake - Llyn Tegid - in Eryri National Park, also known as Snowdonia .

Since 2014, under licence from Natural Resources Wales, Hughes has been wading into the lake to collect and study the snails.

He has designed and installed small concrete shelters for them in the lake itself, and set up his own captive population in a greenhouse at his home in Llanarth.

"Nobody had knowingly seen their eggs before we made that breakthrough," he said.

"You do these things on a wing and a prayer when you're trying to save something that's down to a single site and you're trying to fathom what it needs and how to save it.

Rearing the snails - as well as other critically endangered invertebrates such as scarlet malachite beetles, ladybird spiders and tadpole shrimp - has become a family affair.

"You've got to have a certain mindset to walk out into a freezing cold lake in the middle of January," Ben, 27, explained.

"Every little thing has its place in the ecosystem and if you take a tiny little cog out of any machine it's going to stop working".

The Hughes family is now working with the British and Irish Association of Zoos and Aquariums (BIAZA) to relocate some of their snails to wildlife parks across England.

It is seen as a first step towards restoring them back to locations in the wild over the coming years, as part of a £60m UK government-backed scheme to protect rare species.

"It's such a hugely important conservation project and such a wonderful story," explained Samantha Eden, assistant curator at Wingham Wildlife Park in Kent, who travelled to the Hughes home to pick up 24 glutinous snails.

"We've got a new facility that we've set up for them - three beautiful...
body.zh: 在英国一个湖泊中发现的一只小蜗牛被称为与埃及文物一样珍贵，因为自然资源保护者正在努力拯救它。 英国的几家动物园正在建立所谓的粘性蜗牛种群方舟，粘性蜗牛是欧洲最稀有的物种之一，使用的是在锡尔迪金后花园饲养的生物。 “被它们的可爱所迷惑”，自然资源保护主义者伊恩·休斯将保护这种曾经在英国水域广泛存在的受威胁软体动物作为自己的“生命定义”使命。 “曾经有一段时间，我们花园里的蜗牛比野外看到的还要多，”他说。 Myxas glutinosa 得名于其极其精致、带有金色斑点的棕色外壳上覆盖的粘糊糊的外壳。 它的大小不及指尖，但却拥有大得滑稽的触角——休斯将其比作“松软的大耳朵”。 这种蜗牛以藻类为食，被认为是湖泊和河流健康的指标，但在英格兰各地已被逼至灭绝。 休斯说，这些蜗牛“像埃及文物一样值得保存和珍惜”。 在英国，他们最后的已知避难所是威尔士最大的天然湖 - Llyn Tegid - 位于埃里里国家公园，也称为斯诺登尼亚。 自 2014 年以来，在威尔士自然资源部的许可下，休斯一直涉入湖中收集和研究蜗牛。 他在湖中为它们设计并安装了小型混凝土庇护所，并在拉纳斯家中的温室里安置了自己的圈养种群。 “在我们取得这一突破之前，没有人故意看到他们的鸡蛋，”他说。 “当你试图拯救那些只剩下一个地点的东西，并且试图弄清楚它需要什么以及如何拯救它时，你就可以边祈祷边做这些事情。 饲养蜗牛以及其他极度濒危的无脊椎动物，如猩红孔雀石甲虫、瓢虫蜘蛛和蝌蚪虾，已成为一项家庭事务。 27 岁的本解释说：“在一月中旬走进冰冷的湖水时，你必须有一定的心态。” “每件小事在生态系统中都有自己的位置，如果你从任何机器上取下一个小齿轮，它就会停止工作”。 休斯家族目前正在与英国和爱尔兰动物园和水族馆协会 (BIAZA) 合作，将他们的一些蜗牛转移到英格兰各地的野生动物园。 这被视为未来几年将它们恢复到野外的第一步，也是英国政府支持的 6000 万英镑保护稀有物种计划的一部分。 “这是一个非常重要的保护项目，也是一个非常精彩的故事，”肯特郡温厄姆野生动物公园的助理馆长萨曼莎·伊登 (Samantha Eden) 解释道，她前往休斯家捡了 24 只粘性蜗牛。 “我们为他们建立了一个新设施——三个漂亮的......

reflection.en: The glutinous snail, once common, now clings to existence in a single Welsh lake. Conservationists, like Ian Hughes, dedicate themselves to its survival, finding profound value in this tiny creature. This echoes the ancient wisdom that creation itself speaks volumes, offering insights into the intricate beauty and fragility of life, if only we pause to...
reflection.zh: 曾经随处可见的黏滑蜗牛，如今仅存于威尔士的一个湖泊中，艰难维系着生命。像伊恩·休斯这样的保护主义者，全身心投入到拯救它们的行动中，在这微小的生物身上发现了深刻的价值。这呼应了古老的智慧：受造物本身就蕴含着丰富的启示，它展示了生命的精妙之美与脆弱，只要我们驻足观察，就能从中获得洞见。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: One giant step: first known adult T rex footprints found in North Dakota
title.zh: 巨步：在北达科他州发现已知首批成年霸王龙足迹

summary.en: A 23ft-long trackway, comprising four three-toed footprints (two left, two right) dating back 66.5 million years, has been discovered in North Dakota. This marks the first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex, found by scientists in the Hell Creek Formation.
summary.zh: 在北达科他州发现了一条长达23英尺的足迹，包含四只三趾脚印（两只左脚，两只右脚），距今已有6650万年。这是科学家在地狱溪组（Hell Creek Formation）发现的首批已知的成年霸王龙足迹。

body.en: The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists. The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这条 23 英尺长的足迹由四个三趾脚印组成，两个左两个，右两个，可以追溯到 6650 万年前。一组科学家在北达科他州发现了第一组已知的成年霸王龙脚印。这条 23 英尺长的足迹由四个三趾脚印组成，两个左两个右，去年由科罗拉多州丹佛自然科学博物馆和英国利物浦约翰摩尔斯大学的研究人员首次在该州西南部的地狱溪地层恐龙化石区发现。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The discovery of these ancient T. rex footprints in North Dakota offers a profound glimpse into a world long past. It reminds us that creation itself, from the grandest dinosaur to the smallest creature, testifies to the wisdom and intricate design of its Creator. By studying these traces, we gain a deeper appreciation for the ancient world and the One who...
reflection.zh: 在北达科他州发现的这些古老的霸王龙足迹，让我们得以一窥早已逝去的世界。它提醒我们，整个受造界，从最庞大的恐龙到最小的生灵，都见证着其创造主的智慧和精妙的设计。通过研究这些痕迹，我们能更深刻地体会到古代世界以及那位安排这一切的“雅伟”的伟大。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Weatherwatch: soil moisture deficit – how dry are the UK’s thirsty soils?
title.zh: 天气观察：土壤水分赤字——英国干渴的土壤有多干？

summary.en: Soil Moisture Deficit (SMD) measures how much moisture soil needs to reach its full capacity. Many parts of England and Wales are experiencing very dry conditions, with SMD indicating how much rain is needed to replenish the soil. Drought is often described by meteorologists using SMD, which can range from around...
summary.zh: 土壤水分赤字（SMD）衡量土壤需要多少水分才能达到其最大容量。英格兰和威尔士的大部分地区正经历非常干燥的状况，SMD表明需要多少降雨才能使土壤恢复。气象学家常用SMD来描述干旱，其数值在夏季通常约为100毫米，在干旱年份则可能达到150毫米或更高。

body.en: SMD is the moisture the soil must make up until it is at capacity, with very dry conditions over most of England and Wales When the ground is thoroughly wet, after excess rainwater has run off it is said to be at field capacity. Meteorologists describe drought in terms of soil moisture deficit (SMD) from field capacity. The SMD is a measure of how thirsty the soil is, expressed as how many millimetres of rain it would take to top it up to field capacity. In southern England, the SMD tends to hover around zero in winter when fields are wet. In summer it may be about 100mm, going up to 150mm or more in a dry year. The extreme of dryness, when soil has no water accessible to plants, is known as the permanent wilting point or PWP. Continue reading...
body.zh: SMD 是土壤在达到容量之前必须补充的水分，英格兰和威尔士大部分地区的条件非常干燥。当地面完全湿润时，多余的雨水流失后，就可以说达到了田间容量。气象学家根据田间容量的土壤水分亏缺（SMD）来描述干旱。 SMD 是土壤干渴程度的衡量标准，表示为需要多少毫米的降雨才能达到田间容量。在英格兰南部，冬季田地潮湿时，SMD 往往徘徊在零附近。夏季，水深可能约为 100 毫米，干旱年份可达 150 毫米或更高。当土壤没有水可供植物吸收时，极端干燥被称为永久萎蔫点或 PWP。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The report details the scientific measurement of soil moisture deficit, a way of quantifying the 'thirst' of the land. It's a reminder of the intricate systems of creation, each part playing its role in the grand design. The Psalmist marvels at the abundance and variety of life, recognizing the profound wisdom evident in every aspect of the natural world.
reflection.zh: 报道详细介绍了土壤水分赤字的科学测量方法，这是一种量化土地“口渴”程度的方式。它提醒我们造物拥有精密的系统，每个部分都在宏伟的设计中扮演着自己的角色。诗篇作者惊叹于生命的丰盛与多样，认识到自然界的每个方面都显露出深刻的智慧。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Briefing Chat: The Bunsen burner myth that turns out to be just hot air
title.zh: 简报聊天：事实证明，本生灯的消毒神话不过是些空谈

summary.en: Nature staff discuss an AI tool that can assess the impact of 9 billion mutations—plus, how the Bunsen burner’s reputation for sterilization might be based on tradition alone.
summary.zh: 《自然》杂志的员工讨论了一种可以评估90亿个突变影响的人工智能工具，此外，还探讨了本生灯的消毒声誉可能仅仅基于传统。

reflection.en: The relentless march of scientific discovery, exemplified by an AI tool analyzing billions of mutations, reflects a world where knowledge is rapidly expanding. As we gain unprecedented insights into the natural world, may we also seek the wisdom to use this knowledge for good, remembering that true understanding is rooted in reverence for the Creator.
reflection.zh: 科学发现的不断进步，例如分析数十亿个突变的人工智能工具，反映了一个知识迅速增长的世界。当我们对自然界获得前所未有的见解时，愿我们也寻求智慧，将这些知识用于善事，并牢记真正的理解根植于对造物主的敬畏之中。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: NSF moves to overhaul funding approach in line with White House priorities
title.zh: NSF moves to overhaul funding approach in line with White House priorities

summary.en: The National Science Foundation, a primary funder of basic science, is reportedly planning a significant shift in its funding strategies to align with White House objectives. While the specifics of how these new initiatives will be financed remain undisclosed, there are concerns among staff that this streamlined...
summary.zh: 基础科学的主要资助者美国国家科学基金会（NSF）据报道正计划调整其资助策略，以符合白宫的目标。尽管这些新举措的具体资金来源尚未公布，但工作人员担心这种精简的方针可能会减少对核心科学研究的资助。

reflection.en: The National Science Foundation's proposed overhaul of its funding approach highlights a dynamic where human endeavors to understand the world are constantly evolving. As knowledge expands and priorities shift, the challenge lies in balancing new initiatives with the foundational pursuit of discovery. This echoes the ancient observation that in times of...
reflection.zh: 美国国家科学基金会（NSF）提议对其资助方式进行改革，这凸显了人类探索世界的方式在不断演变的动态。随着知识的扩展和优先事项的转变，挑战在于如何在追求新举措的同时，不忽视基础性的探索发现。这与古老的观察相呼应，即在大发展时期，知识本身也在增长。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: People trust scientists seen to be 'on their side', UK study find
title.zh: 英国研究发现：人们更信任站在“自己一边”的科学家

summary.en: A new report indicates that political leanings and personal values significantly impact public confidence in scientists. The study, published in Nature, suggests that people are more likely to trust scientists they perceive as sharing their own viewpoints or values.
summary.zh: 一份新报告表明，政治倾向和个人价值观显著影响公众对科学家的信任度。这项发表在《自然》杂志上的研究表明，人们更倾向于信任那些他们认为与自己观点或价值观一致的科学家。

reflection.en: This report from Nature suggests that trust in science is not solely based on evidence, but also on perceived alignment with personal values. Proverbs 18:15 reminds us that the pursuit of knowledge is a worthy endeavor, but this story highlights the human element of connection and shared perspective in building confidence.
reflection.zh: 《自然》杂志的这项报告表明，对科学的信任不仅仅基于证据，还基于与个人价值观的感知一致性。箴言18:15提醒我们，追求知识是一项有价值的事业，但这个故事强调了在建立信心时，人际联系和共同视角的要素。

verse.textEn: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, for the ears of the wise seek it out.
verse.textZh: 聪明人的心得知识；智慧人的耳求知识。

title.en: El Niño goes viral — and scientists learn what makes people care about the climate
title.zh: 厄尔尼诺现象病毒式传播——科学家们了解到人们为何关心气候变化

summary.en: Evoking emotions is more likely to prompt people to engage with climate efforts than are data alone.
summary.zh: 激发情感比单纯的数据更能促使人们参与气候行动。

reflection.en: This research suggests that connecting with people's hearts, not just their minds, is key to motivating climate action. As Philippians 4:8 reminds us, we should focus our thoughts on what is true, noble, right, pure, lovely, admirable, excellent, and praiseworthy. When we engage with climate issues through this lens, focusing on the beauty of creation and...
reflection.zh: 这项研究表明，与人们的心灵沟通，而不仅仅是头脑，是推动气候行动的关键。正如腓立比书 4:8 所提醒我们的，我们应当思念地上凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的。当我们透过这个视角来关注气候问题，专注于造物的之美以及我们守护它的责任时，我们就能超越纯粹的数据，激发有意义的改变。

verse.textEn: Whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable — think about such things.
verse.textZh: 凡是真实的、可敬的、公义的、清洁的、可爱的、有美名的，这些事你们都要思念。

title.en: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
title.zh: 前Anthropic研究员告诉BBC：人工智能员工“真心害怕”人类的未来

summary.en: An AI researcher who quit Anthropic told the BBC that people working on the technology are "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.
summary.zh: 一位从Anthropic辞职的人工智能研究员告诉BBC，从事这项技术的人们对它的快速发展及其对人类的潜在影响“真心感到恐惧”。

body.en:
An artificial intelligence researcher who quit AI firm Anthropic has said people working on the technology were "genuinely frightened" about the speed of its advancements and what it could mean for humanity.

Jacob Coxon told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg on Saturday about his viral resignation post in which he raised concerns about out-of-control AI.

"I believe that if we don't slow down at the current rate of progress, there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future," he said.

His resignation comes amid growing safety concerns in the industry, including from his former boss, Anthropic head Dario Amodei, who in an essay argued for development to slow down.

The bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk of xAI, have both said they agree with Amodei's proposal for industry-wide deceleration and regulation, as well as independent monitoring of AI model development.

Amodei said developing the technology was not in question, but the risks associated with it were "serious", and that companies and governments must be given time to address them.

The 27-year-old Coxon - who worked at OpenAI before joining Anthropic - welcomed the suggestion of a slowdown but said it would need to be co-ordinated with China to avoid "a race at an international scale".

"The people who work at these companies are completely serious when they ask for regulation because they find themselves trapped in a race. And they're scared of the outcomes of that race," he told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

The hardest question to answer, according to Coxon, was what an AI apocalypse would look like.

One of the risks outlined in Amodei's comments was of a swarm of bots acting like a supercomputer that could take over the internet.

In response to Coxon's departure, an Anthropic spokesperson told BBC News: "We have always been transparent that AI will bring both enormous benefits and unprecedented risks.

"To address these risks, we continue to build models with some of the strongest safeguards in the industry."

The firm has been a pioneer in studying how AI models work, the spokesperson added. It was the first to publish a framework for mitigating the risks posed by their development - and it also "aggressively" tests its models and publishes the findings to aid scrutiny and prevent incidents of "AI misalignment".

"This work is also why we believe the world would benefit from the industry adopting a lawful, verifiable way to work together to pace how we release powerful models," they said.

Industry figures have suggested comments about the perils and power of AI may be designed to generate hype. Other critics say Anthropic has been trying to trigger a regulatory push to block competition, leaving it and OpenAI with a duopoly.

Anthropic...
body.zh: 一位退出 Anthropic 的人工智能研究人员告诉 BBC，从事这项技术的人们“真的害怕”它的进步速度以及它对人类的意义。 周六，雅各布·考克森 (Jacob Coxon) 接受了英国广播公司 (BBC) 的劳拉·昆斯伯格 (Laura Kuenssberg) 采访，谈论了他的病毒式辞职帖子，他在帖子中提出了对人工智能失控的担忧。 “我相信，如果我们不按照目前的进展速度放慢速度，我们很有可能在不久的将来都会死去，”他说。 他辞职之际，该行业的安全担忧日益严重，其中包括他的前老板、Anthropic 公司负责人达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei)，他在周六的一篇文章中主张放慢发展速度。 然而，一些行业人士表示，这种危险被夸大了，可能是为了在这两家最大的人工智能公司潜在上市之前进行炒作，或者是为了促进监管，从而减缓其竞争对手的步伐。 27 岁的英国人 Coxon 的研究重点是训练人工智能模型，他表示，包括埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 OpenAI 的萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 在内的人工智能领导者也与阿莫迪有着类似的担忧。 “他们都发表了关于必须警惕人工智能接管的可能性的声明。他们都谈到了这一点。人工智能接管意味着人类灭绝，”考克森说。 考克森表示，最难回答的问题是它会是什么样子。 考克森说：“你可以提出的任何具体场景最终听起来都像科幻小说。”但他指出，已经发生的进步在过去听起来就像小说。 考克森说，一种潜在的情况可能是人工智能代理侵入医学实验室，“自主生产致命病毒”。他列出的另一个例子可能是人工智能入侵“世界运行的关键基础设施”。 研究人员指出 OpenAI 最近的一份报告，该报告详细介绍了其自己的技术如何对名为 Hugging Face 的在线平台进行黑客攻击。 考克森说：“他们是自主完成的，没有任何人为鼓励。他们选择继续这种黑客热潮。事情变得越来越快，事情也变得越来越可怕。” 阿莫迪的评论中概述的风险之一是一群机器人像超级计算机一样可以接管互联网。 据报道，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 正在为可能创纪录的首次公开募股做准备。行业人士表示，有关人工智能的危险和力量的评论可能旨在引起炒作。其他批评者表示，Anthropic 一直试图引发监管推动阻止竞争，使其和 OpenAI 形成双寡头垄断。 Coxon的观点也遭到了AI平台Hugging Face首席执行官Clement Delangue的质疑。 “抱歉，但是向雅各布询问人工智能......

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI, as described by a former Anthropic researcher, raises profound questions about human ambition and foresight. The biblical story of Babel warns against unchecked human endeavors that, while seemingly unified and powerful, can lead to unintended and chaotic consequences when divorced from divine wisdom. This echoes the fear that...
reflection.zh: 正如一位前Anthropic研究员所描述的，人工智能的飞速发展引发了关于人类野心和远见的深刻问题。圣经中关于巴别塔的故事告诫人们，那些看似统一而强大的、不受约束的人类努力，如果脱离了神的智慧，可能会导致意想不到的混乱后果。这与人们对人工智能不受控制的进步可能超越我们明智引导能力，从而带来生存风险的恐惧不谋而合。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: The AfD won a shock election in Germany. Elon Musk was thrilled

Billionaire Elon Musk expressed his enthusiasm for this outcome, suggesting a symbiotic relationship between him and...
summary.zh: 德国另类选择党（AfD）在本周的德国州选举中取得了令人瞩目的胜利，使其距离组建自二战以来德国首个由极右翼领导的州政府仅一步之遥。亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克对这一结果表示兴奋，暗示了他与该党之间存在一种共生关系，旨在同时在德国和美国传播其极右翼观点。

Elon Musk was thrilled. Continue reading...

Proverbs 29:2 warns that when the wicked gain power, the people groan. This verse calls us to be discerning about the leaders we elevate and the ideologies we amplify, praying for wisdom and justice to prevail in...
reflection.zh: 德国另类选择党（AfD）的崛起，并得到埃隆·马斯克等知名人士的喝彩，鲜明地提醒我们政治格局可能发生怎样的变化。《箴言》29章2节警告说，恶人掌权，百姓就叹息。这节经文呼吁我们要辨别所推崇的领导者和所宣扬的意识形态，并为国家事务中的智慧和公义祈祷。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

These scam websites offer the latest models at significantly lower prices than official retailers, enticing buyers who are put off by the high cost of new releases. Victims...

But you balk at the £1,199 price tag for the cheapest of the new options. Searching online for a better price with the words “cheap”, “iPhone” and “deal”, you come across a website which offers an iPhone 18 Pro for a couple of hundred pounds less than the Apple site. You pay for the new phone via a bank transfer and wait for it to arrive. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The allure of a bargain can be powerful, especially when it comes to coveted technology like the latest iPhone. However, this story highlights how the desire for a 'deal' can blind people to red flags, leading them into the hands of those who exploit greed. The pursuit of material gain, whether by scammers or their victims, often leads to spiritual and...
reflection.zh: 优惠的诱惑力可能很大，尤其是对于像最新款iPhone这样令人垂涎的科技产品。然而，这个故事表明，对“交易”的渴望会让人忽视危险信号，落入那些利用贪婪之徒的圈套。追求物质利益，无论是诈骗者还是受害者，往往会导致精神和经济上的损失。

verse.textEn: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
verse.textZh: 贪财是万恶之根。

title.en: OpenAI IPO will not happen in 2026 amid AI safety fears, Sam Altman says
title.zh: 传闻OpenAI将在2026年上市，萨姆·奥特曼表示担忧人工智能安全
